action: General advice: Iris Plaza customers should change their password there and anywhere they reused it, and watch for messages pretending to be from the shop; Iris Plaza says it will contact those affected individually by email and other means.
date_note: Day Iris Plaza announced the possible leak and its figures (second report), per Netshop Impress and ScanNetSecurity. A suspicious file was found on 28 October and unauthorised access was announced on 29 October. Earlier this record used 12 November, the end of a weekly roundup.

evidence.quote: 対象データは、会員約580万人分と非会員約190万人分の計約770万人分。
アイリスオーヤマ公式通販サイト「アイリスプラザ」に不正アクセス、約770万人の個人情報が漏えいした可能性

exec: An online retailer says data of about 7.7 million people, including encrypted passwords, may have leaked from an external cloud service.
plain: Iris Plaza, which runs Iris Ohyama's official online shop in Japan, says personal data of about 7.7 million people may have leaked from an outside cloud service. Card details were not stored there.
summary: Iris Plaza, which runs Iris Ohyama's official online shop, said on 5 November that data of about 5.8 million members and about 1.9 million non-members, about 7.7 million in total, may have leaked after unauthorised access to an external cloud service. Member data may include names, addresses, emails, gender, passwords (stored encrypted) and birth dates; card data was not affected, Netshop Impress reports. The actual number is still under investigation.
title: Iris Ohyama's Iris Plaza shop: data of about 7.7 million people may have leaked from cloud service

validation.note: Follow-up: Netshop Impress (9 Nov) and ScanNetSecurity (16 Nov) each report Iris Plaza's 5 November second report with about 7.7 million people; Netshop Impress gives the member/non-member split, data items, encrypted passwords, unaffected card data and the 29 October reports to police and the PPC. Iris Ohyama's own release (irisohyama.co.jp/news/2026/1105.pdf) answered 403 and was not read. The Privacy Guides roundup was dropped as a source.
